verdict: Sales rose just 1% because an $85M tariff-refund accrual for customers cut the top line, but profit more than doubled versus a year ago that was hit by a large impairment charge.

segments.name: Intelligent Devices
segments.note: Factory hardware: drives, controllers and other smart devices.

segments.name: Software & Control
segments.note: Software and control systems that run factories — the fastest-growing segment.

segments.name: Lifecycle Services
segments.note: Services, maintenance and projects over a plant's life; reported sales fell because of divestitures, while organic sales rose 2%.

segments.name: Unallocated — customer tariff refunds
segments.note: An $85M accrual for refunds to customers of tariff-related price increases, recorded as a reduction of sales and not allocated to any segment.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, marketing and running the company; includes a $50M charitable contribution and restructuring charges.

opex.name: Engineering and development
opex.note: Engineering and developing new automation products and software.

follow100Note: The unallocated tariff-refund segment is negative, so the three business segments add to more than $100 of every $100 before that $85M reduction. Other income is negative because interest expense ($33M) was larger than other income ($11M). Segment percentages sum to 100.01 due to rounding to two decimal places.

takeaways.title: Software & Control led growth
takeaways.text: Software & Control sales rose 15% to $754M and Intelligent Devices rose 5% to $1.14B, while Lifecycle Services fell 9% on divestitures.

takeaways.title: Tariff refunds cut both ways
takeaways.text: Rockwell received $103M of IEEPA tariff refunds, which lowered cost of sales, but also accrued $85M to refund customers for tariff price increases, which lowered sales. The net effect added $0.11 to EPS.

takeaways.title: Net income was $346M
takeaways.text: Net income attributable to Rockwell was $346M, or $3.11 per share, up from $138M a year earlier when results included a $224M goodwill and intangible impairment.

oneTimers: $103M of IEEPA tariff refunds (plus $5M of related interest) reduced cost of sales in the quarter.
An $85M accrual for the customer tariff refund program reduced sales in the quarter.
A $50M contribution to the Rockwell Automation Charitable Corporation and $25M of restructuring charges were recorded in the quarter.
footerNote: Fiscal year ends September 30, so this is the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026. Other income of -$22M is other income of $11M minus interest expense of $33M. Segment sales in the release total $2,417M before the unallocated $85M customer tariff refund accrual, which is shown as its own segment row here so the segments sum exactly to reported sales.
